-module(distribution_pending_probe).
-export([run/0]).

run() ->
    Node = pending_probe@localhost,
    H1 = {Id, Ref} = erts_internal:new_connection(Node),
    true = is_integer(Id),
    true = is_reference(Ref),
    true = Id >= 0 andalso Id =< 16#ffffff,
    H2 = erts_internal:new_connection(Node),
    true = H1 =:= H2,
    S0 = erlang:dist_get_stat(H1),
    io:format(standard_error, "pending_stat=~p~n", [S0]),
    High = classify(fun() -> erlang:dist_get_stat({Id + (1 bsl 32), Ref}) end),
    Low = classify(fun() -> erlang:dist_get_stat({Id - (1 bsl 32), Ref}) end),
    Big = classify(fun() -> erlang:dist_get_stat({1 bsl 59, Ref}) end),
    WrongRef = classify(fun() -> erlang:dist_get_stat({Id, make_ref()}) end),
    true = erts_internal:abort_pending_connection(Node, H1),
    true = erts_internal:abort_pending_connection(Node, H1),
    H3 = {Next, Ref3} = erts_internal:new_connection(Node),
    true = Next =:= ((Id + 1) band 16#ffffff),
    true = Ref =:= Ref3,
    Stale = classify(fun() -> erlang:dist_get_stat(H1) end),
    Current = classify(fun() -> erlang:dist_get_stat(H3) end),
    true = erts_internal:abort_pending_connection(Node, H1),
    true = erts_internal:abort_pending_connection(Node, H3),
    {ok, flat_typed_handle, same_pending_identity, next_connection_id,
     High, Low, Big, WrongRef, Stale, Current}.

classify(F) ->
    try F() of Value -> {ok, Value}
    catch Class:Reason -> {Class, Reason}
    end.

## Dated correction to closed Part267 audit

The earlier audit wording `{ConnectionId,DHandle}` for erts_internal:new_connection/1 can imply an extra nesting level. Actual native dist.c:5588-5624 returns the flat dhandle itself: `{ConnectionId, MagicDistEntryReference}`, built by erl_node_tables.c:400-409. The internal Erlang typespec's dist_handle wording is not the C return-shape authority. Closed Part267 evidence remains unchanged; this is a dated source correction. Native abort_pending_connection/2 returns not-was-connected (dist.c:5693-5710), including true for idle or stale IDs, not a boolean indicating a transition.

## Implemented source prerequisite

A lazy runtime-owned table shares ProcessRuntime's exact membership/lifetime gate. Four existing files change: ProcessRuntime.cs only synchronous death and dispose hooks, ProcessRuntime.Halt.cs a close hook, RuntimeReferenceResources.cs the partial declaration, ReferenceResourceKind.cs a distinct DistributionEntry payload kind. No constructor/node/creation properties or loader/Core code are imported or changed. New partial files add table creation and strongly typed resource create/acquire. Resource payload guards do not acquire the runtime gate while the resource gate is held: new paths order RuntimeGate -> ResourceGate -> ResourceEntryGate, and leases release resource admission before obtaining table snapshots.

Pending entries have native flat two-tuple handle shape, genuine typed resource identity (not HOST handle or a marker-only reference), stable resource through idle/pending transitions, a24-bit ID incremented only IDLE->PENDING, weak idle identity retention and strong pending ownership. The initialization seed uses a local monotonic counter's low24 bits, not an exact native clock equality claim. Finite configurable node metadata budget is a HOST tuning policy, not OTP's native allocation limit. Stale handle acquisition rejects IDs; native small tagged values are constrained to the pinned64-bit range derived from erl_term.h tag4 bits and SMALL_BITS, then truncated to uint32 as native dhandle parsing does. High/negative alias native observations remain pending.

Kernel/controller roles are explicit SETUP RESERVATIONS only. Kernel setup requires a real live registered net_kernel ProcessContext; controllers are real distinct owned live processes with one reserved pending entry. This does NOT establish the native local distribution entry/F_DISTRIBUTION role required by setnode/3; Root's local-identity/native kernel admission work remains prerequisite. Reserving a role never produces connected state or native get_opt/get_data authority. Kernel release/death aborts pending reservations, controller death aborts its reservation synchronously before process Done is completed, and runtime halt/disposal closes all entries and resource payloads under the runtime gate. Hooks are idempotent. The separate published caller-owned HOST queue manager remains unchanged.

Snapshots describe IDLE/PENDING/CLOSED metadata and reserved owner PIDs only. There are no fabricated native packet, memory or queue statistics. HOST AbortPending is a strict transition operation, deliberately not the native internal wrapper's return contract. Existing ETF saved-identity/factory behavior is reused with strict owner/kind checks; its published-identity and creation-zero foundation scope is inherited, not promoted to complete native resources. Foreign/wrong-kind/plain marker refs reject acquisition. Live owner-aware ETF copies can regain typed authority after Save; closed resources fall back to plain reference identity.

Unexecuted focused source checks cover flat shape, repeated identity/ID, namespace validation, explicit finite budget, live ETF restore and foreign fallback, wrong kinds and plain marker rejection, exact24-bit increment, source-derived small-int aliases, lease staleness/disposal, registered kernel/controller reservations, synchronous death cleanup while old callback remains blocked, distinct replacement,32 kernel-release/reacquire loops, halt quiescence and ordinary disposal. The native probe is independently predeclared UNEXECUTED source only; native packet/transport parity is not inferred from a future pending-state projection. Build, source peer review and actual focused results must be appended separately.
